3.text: speak the human language. I really had a knife on my belt; and a Russian

4.text: cossack who sat next me proposed laughingly that I give it to Akɪˊmlᴀkê.

5.text: Hearing this, the women of the house raised a frightened cry. Akɪˊmlᴀkê,

6.text: however, who doubtless was stung by the taunt implied in the words of the

7.text: cossack, suddenly picked up from the ground a long, sharp-pointed chip of

8.text: wood, and, baring his abdomen, put one end of the stick on his body, and

9.text: the other against my breast. Then he made a thrust forward with the whole

10.text: weight of his heavy body. The chip, of course, was snapped in two. One

11.text: end flew up and hit me on the brow very near to the left eye, leaving an

12.text: ugly gash. The other end cut a deep scratch entirely across the abdomen

13.text: of Akɪˊmlᴀkê. I wonder that it had not been driven in. All this was done

14.text: so quick that nobody had time to interfere.

15.text: Akɪˊmlᴀkê with much coolness picked up a handful of snow, and, wiping

16.text: off the blood from his abdomen, quietly went to another tent. In half an

17.text: hour, when he was no longer thirsting for blood, I asked him about his

18.text: actions; but he disclaimed all knowledge, and expressed the utmost wonder

19.text: when showed the bloody scratch on his own abdomen.

20.text: This incident is quite characteristic of the shamans of all primitive people,

21.text: because it represents a blending of ecstatic excitement with daring and cool

22.text: deceit, which is able to lead them to quite unexpected actions.

23.text: We have already mentioned¹ that in the thanksgiving ceremonial, as in

24.text: many others, the day performance in the outer tent, with its special incidents,

25.text: ends during the night-time in the inner room, with the usual shamanistic

26.text: seance, which lasts frequently until broad daylight. Whenever several shamans

27.text: are present, a contest takes place in both the outer and the inner tent.

31.text: Chukchee folk-lore is full of detailed descriptions of such contests, and

32.text: even of extemporaneous matches to which two men of power invite each

33.text: other, and which are said to last often for several months.

35.text: Russianized natives. The details of all these stories, however, are mostly of
